doc.title: Ellis Marsalis — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Final words and tombstone joke
summary: He has nothing to add and jokes about the Jazz Master title.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: “Stomp off, let’s go.” All right. Do you have anything else you’d like to contribute to the historical record?
Once again, as the patriarch of the first family of jazz . . .
Oh boy. Patriarch of the first family of jazz.
I’m sure that’s how it’s going to read on the NEA Jazz Masters Award, however. But we’ll know you as Ellis Marsalis, the pianist, educator, and father.
If I ever make a will out, I’m going to put that in there: “Do not put that on my tombstone.”
What do you want on your tombstone?
Zero. And they don’t bury people here, so . . .
I mean, they don’t bury them underground. They bury them, of course.
They got all of these vaults and stuff.
Yeah, we got a couple of those.
